answer: Because the kernel nonce is published only after close, the fable audit can verify each derivation and a shared text is provable as copied. The three words are derived from a 101 bit value mixing the epoch seed with the identity key, so no two keys ever receive the same triple. That removes the entire premise of a template farm, which depends on one text serving many identities, and forces a separate sonnet derivation per key. That is 8 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
